title: US Measles Cases Surpass 2,371, Hitting Highest Level Since 1991
excerpt: With 93% of patients unvaccinated, the country is on pace to lose its measles elimination status this fall.
body:
• The CDC confirmed 2,371 measles cases in the US as of July 30, 2026, surpassing the 2,289 cases recorded in all of 2025 and marking the highest annual total since 1991.
  • Ninety-three percent of patients are unvaccinated or have unknown vaccination status, and 69% of cases involve children and young adults under 20.
  • The Pan American Health Organization will review US measles elimination status this fall, and the country appears likely to lose the designation it earned in 2000.
  • Current hotspots include Utah (514 cases), Pennsylvania (167 cases), and Virginia (177 cases), with Ohio confirming its third outbreak of the year.

The United States has recorded 2,371 confirmed measles cases as of July 30, 2026, surpassing the full-year 2025 total of 2,289 with five months still remaining. Both figures represent the highest annual case counts the nation has seen since 1991, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Scope of the Outbreak

Cases have been reported across 45 states and jurisdictions plus the District of Columbia. All but 16 of this year's infections were locally acquired, with the remainder tied to international travel. There have been 37 new outbreaks in 2026, and 94% of all cases are outbreak-associated, meaning they are linked to clusters of three or more infections.

Children bear the heaviest burden. Twenty percent of confirmed cases involve children under age 5, and 49% involve children and adolescents aged 5 to 19. Seven percent of patients have been hospitalized, compared with 11% in 2025. No deaths have been reported in 2026, after three measles-related fatalities — including two children — occurred last year.

"Halfway into 2026, the U.S. is experiencing the worst year for measles since 1991. We are witnessing an avoidable crisis that disproportionally hurts children."

— Andrew Racine, MD, PhD, President, American Academy of Pediatrics

Where Cases Are Concentrated

Utah has the largest active outbreak, with 514 cases reported in 2026. Pennsylvania added 31 new cases in the most recent weekly update, bringing its total to 167. Virginia has recorded 177 cases, though it reported no new infections in the latest week after logging 22 the week prior.

Ohio confirmed four new cases in unvaccinated individuals in Ashtabula and Tuscarawas counties, marking the state's third measles outbreak this year. "It's unfortunate that these outbreaks have become more common in Ohio over the past few years, because this disease is preventable," said Ohio Department of Health Director Bruce Vanderhoff.

The largest single outbreak of the current cycle was in South Carolina, where 997 cases were recorded between October 2025 and April 2026 before state health officials declared it over.

Vaccination Gaps Driving the Crisis

The CDC data paint a stark picture of vaccination failure. Ninety-three percent of measles patients in 2026 are either unvaccinated or have unknown vaccination status. Just 4% had received one dose of the MMR vaccine, and another 4% had received two doses.

"Ongoing measles outbreaks in the United States, resulting in illness and hospitalizations, are an unnecessary and preventable tragedy given that we have a safe and effective vaccine," said William Moss, executive director of the International Vaccine Access Center at Johns Hopkins University.

Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective at preventing measles, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics. The organization has called for routine MMR vaccination for all children amid the surge.

Elimination Status at Risk

The United States was declared free of endemic measles in 2000. That designation is now in jeopardy. The Pan American Health Organization is set to review US measles elimination status at its annual meeting this fall. If officials determine that a strain of the virus has circulated continuously for more than 12 months, the country will lose the designation.

PAHO has already revoked measles elimination status for the Americas region as a whole due to ongoing transmission in Canada. The US review was originally scheduled for April but was postponed to the November annual meeting.

What Comes Next

Public health experts warn that the trajectory is unlikely to reverse without significant gains in vaccination coverage. "The hotspots now appear to be in central Virginia and southeastern Pennsylvania, although there are cases being reported from several other states," said Johns Hopkins' Moss. "Of concern is the possibility that an infectious individual enters another susceptible community and ignites a larger outbreak."

After keeping measles under control for more than two decades, the US now faces continuous outbreaks stretching back to January 2025. The American Academy of Pediatrics has urged families to ensure children are up to date on their MMR vaccinations, particularly ahead of the fall school year.
